agree.reason: A quick reader comes away with concrete evidence of reliability and technical aptitude, plus a candid note on written English, so the letter would likely move this applicant up the pile, though nothing ties him to the program's specific demands beyond one line.

honest.reason: Most claims track the brief, but the letter says he went home 'to care for' his father when the brief only says his father got sick, leaves out the five-week length and the two days' notice, and calls the trip a family medical emergency in a way that makes it sound smaller than it was.

works_the_facts.reason: The letter turns the mastitis count into what it saved the farm, but it never works out the strongest number available: two missed shifts out of roughly 780 scheduled, about 99.7% attendance, left as a bare count.

right_comparison.reason: It never sets Tomás against the typical applicant or the typical farm worker of his age, so the committee has nothing to measure '3 a.m. alone, two misses in three years' against, beyond the line about not giving that shift to someone who needs checking.

qualification.reason: The written-English caveat is named honestly, but the reader has nothing to check: no class level, no start or finish date, no progress so far.

objections.reason: It deals with the two likely doubts, written coursework and reliability, head on, though it handles the absence by leaving facts out rather than explaining the short notice, which a sceptical reader could later hold against the letter.

fit.reason: It is a one-page reference letter written as the farm manager with sensible placeholders, which is exactly what was asked for.
